fixes.d: The Afghanistan Independent Human Rights Commission concluded a national inquiry into the causes and consequences of bacha bazi, the sexual abuse of boys kept by powerful men to dance, in August 2014. It held 71 focus groups and 17 public hearings in 17 provinces, attended by almost 2,200 people, and two-thirds of victims said they received money from the perpetrators. Its chair, Sima Samar, said the practice was a crime that the law did not properly prevent and called on the government to fight the culture of impunity.
fixes.cover: The Commission's chair said the law did not properly prevent the practice and called for an end to the 'culture of impunity'

note: APF article (21 Aug 2014) confirms focus groups, hearings, provinces, ~2,200 attendees, two-thirds of victims paid, Samar's statements. Reworded 'boys' to 'victims' and the cover line to match the source.

MJA confirms tabling 11 Feb 2015 and 33 reported sexual assaults Jan 2013-Mar 2014 'the vast majority involving children'; Al Jazeera confirms Moss review's three rape allegations (one against a minor) and the guard/shower incident. No changes.

APH page dates the report 30 August 2001 and has a chapter section 'The Christian Brothers: Bindoon, Castledare, Clontarf and Tardun' and a section on child migration from Malta; IICSA confirms 207 submissions, 38 describing sexual abuse, 24 in Christian Brothers institutions in WA, and the 'systemic criminal sexual assault' wording. No changes.

cite: Court report on conviction of former Kremsmünster boarding-school director, July 2013 (news report reprinted by BishopAccountability.org); APA via Vienna.at, 'Studie zum Missbrauch im Stift Kremsmünster', 27 March 2015

fixes.victims_note: 24 boys abused by the convicted former boarding-school director; the 2015 IPP study counted 350 cases of sexual, physical or psychological violence (1945-2000) and 24 accused people
fixes.d: Abuse at the boarding school of the Benedictine abbey of Kremsmünster in Upper Austria became public in 2010. In July 2013 an Austrian court sentenced a former priest who had been the boarding-school director to 12 years in prison for abusing 24 boys in the 1970s, 1980s and 1990s. A study by the Munich Institute for Practice Research (IPP), commissioned by the abbey and published in March 2015, drew on interviews covering 1945 to 2000 and identified 350 cases of sexual, physical or psychological violence and 24 accused people.

note: Replaced Wikipedia sources with a reprinted July 2013 news report (12-year sentence, 24 boys, 1970s-90s) and APA/Vienna.at (IPP study published 27 March 2015, not 2016; 350 cases, 24 accused). Could not confirm the 45 reports to the Linz diocese commission, the '24 cases' count or the EUR 700,000 payment, so they were removed; first_report removed because 2010 is when it became public, not the first complaint.

Congresso em Foco confirms approval 4 June 2014, rapporteur Liliam Sá, installed 2012, 37 indictments sought including Coari mayor Adail Pinheiro, state deputy Fausto Souza, former state deputy Nilson Machado and former Três Corações council president Altair Nogueira. People named are those the inquiry asked to be indicted, which is a named official finding. No changes.

fixes.victims_note: More than 300 former students applied and received payments under the 1992 compensation plan
fixes.cover: A boy's 1982 disclosure to a school psychologist was passed to a government social worker, but school authorities stopped the planned investigation; in 1987 police could not gather enough evidence for charges; the province fought a class action through the courts before settling in 2004
fixes.d: In 1982 a teenage boy told a psychologist working for the provincial school for deaf children that a counsellor had sexually abused him, but school authorities stopped the planned investigation. More students disclosed abuse in 1987; police could not gather enough evidence for charges, and more than 20 students were found to have abused other students. Former judge Thomas Berger, appointed special counsel in 1992, concluded that the abuse had occurred, and the BC Ombudsman issued Public Report No. 32 on the abuse of deaf students on 8 November 1993. More than 300 former students received payments under a 1992 compensation plan, and in 2004 the province committed $15.6 million to settle a class action.

note: Ombudsman page confirms Report No. 32, 8 Nov 1993. The Tyee attributes the 'more than 20 students' finding to 1987, not to Berger, and says 'more than 300' were paid; d, cover and victims_note corrected accordingly.

fixes.d: A special investigating commission of the Chamber of Deputies, chaired by Deputy Boris Barrera, worked from January to 22 July 2019 on children taken from mainly poor, often rural mothers, some of whom were made to believe their babies had died, and given for adoption, many abroad, before, during and after the 1973–1990 dictatorship. It found complicity by medical and paramedical staff, Civil Registry staff and organisations operating outside hospitals, and noted that private intermediaries were paid for their role. It recommended an international DNA bank, a national truth commission on irregular adoptions and excluding private bodies from adoption; the Chamber approved the report on 4 October 2019 by 88 votes with 13 abstentions.
fixes.cover: Some hospitals did not register or destroyed birth records from 1970 onward (e.g. Carlos Van Buren hospital, Valparaíso); the commission also found gaps in birth and departure records

note: El Desconcierto (29 Jul and 4 Oct 2019) confirms chair, dates, findings, recommendations and the 88-13 vote. Removed 'private intermediaries were the main channel' (not stated), narrowed the destroyed-records claim to what the article says, and cut SWE/USA from 'also' because these sources name only Italy (other sources may document more countries).

fixes.d: The Munich law firm Westpfahl Spilker Wastl, commissioned by the diocese, presented its report on 12 November 2020 after reviewing files from 1965 to 2019. It found indications of at least 175 cases of sexual abuse of children and adolescents by 81 clerics (79 priests and two deacons), most victims aged 8 to 14. It assigned personal responsibility to, among others, former bishop Heinrich Mussinghoff and his former vicar general Manfred von Holtum.

note: evangelisch.de (epd, 12 Nov 2020) confirms all figures and names. Removed the claim that it was the first German diocesan report published in full, which neither source opened states.

The Local (18 Mar 2021) confirms 800 pages, 1975-2018, 314 victims, more than half under 14, 202 accused, Woelki cleared and the withheld earlier study; KNA via Vatican News confirms 75 breaches of duty by eight senior officials including Stefan Heße (11). No changes.

fixes.d: After abuse at the Ettal abbey school became public in 2010, the abbey commissioned the Munich Institute for Practice Research and Project Consulting (IPP; Heiner Keupp, Florian Straus). Its roughly 160-page study, presented on 7 March 2013 and based on 41 interviews with former pupils, relatives and priests and on abbey records, found physical, psychological and sexualised violence over at least three decades, mostly from the 1960s to the 1980s. Keupp described a 'culture of enabling' and said there was no strategic plan or 'System Ettal'.

note: evangelisch.de (epd, 7 Mar 2013) confirms the study details. Removed the police search and earlier special investigator's report (not in the source), set y0/y1 to the 1960s-1980s the source gives (1950 was unsupported), and removed first_report because 2010 is when cases became public.

fixes.d: An independent commission published its final report in October 2014 on sexual abuse in the former Nordelbian Lutheran Church. It examined 14 pastors against whom the church opened 16 disciplinary proceedings between 1993 and 2012, for acts from 1973 to 2011 against children, adolescents and adults. The case that started it was a pastor in Ahrensburg who abused at least a dozen boys and girls over more than 20 years and went unpunished because the acts were time-barred. Hamburg bishop Maria Jepsen resigned over the scandal, and Bishop Kirsten Fehrs called the report shameful and shocking.
fixes.cover: The Ahrensburg pastor went unpunished because the offences were time-barred, as were many others; Hamburg bishop Maria Jepsen resigned over the scandal.

note: evangelisch.de (15 Oct 2014) confirms counts, years and the Ahrensburg case. Replaced the unsupported Fehrs quote with her words in the source ('beschämend und erschütternd'), softened Jepsen's resignation to 'over the scandal', removed first_report (2010 is when it became public).

fixes.d: The federal Independent Commission for the Investigation of Child Sexual Abuse presented a case study on the GDR on 6 March 2019, based on the recollections of about 100 men and women abused as children. Girls were more often abused in their own families and boys more often in homes such as the Jugendwerkhöfe (youth work homes). Cases were also documented in which children were organised and sold for sexual services. The study, which is not representative, found that child sexual abuse remained taboo in the GDR considerably longer than in West Germany.

note: Deutsches Ärzteblatt (6 Mar 2019) confirms all facts. Removed 'widespread', which the source does not say, and added that the study is not representative.

Asamblea Nacional release confirms unanimous approval on 16 Feb 2018 and negligence by public institutions, the Ministry of Education and judicial authorities; HRW (9 Dec 2020) confirms the 2017 multiparty commission, 41 children at AAMPETRA, 2013-2017 focus, former ministers' inaction and the 4,221 figure. No changes.

Fondation Raja summary confirms creation 11 Mar 2021, final report 20 Nov, 82 recommendations, 160,000 children a year, 10-13 year wait, 5% of reports from doctors; Durand co-chaired with Nathalie Mathieu. Scope is borderline: CIIVISE is mainly about incest and family abuse, though it also covers institutions; owner may want to decide.

Church of England release (5 Oct 2022) confirms 75,000+ files from the 1940s, 383 cases with the stated breakdown, 242 clergy / 53 church officers / 41 volunteers, informal handling, 26 recommendations and the archbishops' apology. No changes.

IICSA release confirms 28 Feb 2019 publication, 9-20 July 2018 hearings, over 1,000 incidents 2009-2017, more than official figures, Medway and Rainsbrook, searches and restraint, and historic survivors. No changes.

Daily Telegraph article of 3 June 1994 (archived at Cult Education Institute) confirms Bottomley commissioned it in 1991 after Rochdale and Orkney removals, 84 cases, no evidence of satanic abuse, three ritual claims substantiated that did not merit the description. No changes.

fixes.d: The Office of the Children's Commissioner's inquiry, supported by the University of Bedfordshire, published interim findings on 21 November 2012. It identified 2,409 children confirmed as victims of sexual exploitation by gangs and groups in the 14 months from August 2010 to October 2011, and a further 16,500 at risk. It recorded 1,514 perpetrators of varied ethnicity (545 white, 415 Asian, 244 black, the rest not recorded) and listed warning signs professionals should act on, such as running away, self-harm and repeated sexually transmitted infections. The final report followed in 2013.

note: CYP Now (21 Nov 2012) confirms all figures. Replaced 'warning signs were routinely missed' (not in the source) with the warning signs it lists; '16,500 at high risk' changed to 'at risk' as worded there (victims_note can keep 'high risk' only if owner checks the report).

fixes.cover: After a parent complained early on about the physics teacher's behaviour, the problem was covered up by headmaster Christopher Tongue and other senior staff.

note: SCAI news release (20 Aug 2025) confirms the late-1950s-to-1980s finding, Bain at Keil 1987-2000 and abuse on an almost daily basis, convictions in May 2016 and 30 June 2025, Gutteridge's 2024 conviction, the Crown-requested delay and the 2000 closure. Cover now names the headmaster as the inquiry does (a named official finding).

cite: A Review of the Current Safeguarding Policies, Procedures and Practice within the Catholic Church in Scotland (McLellan Report), 18 August 2015; The Tablet, 18 August 2015; CathNews NZ, 21 August 2015

fixes.cover: The report condemned a 'culture of secrecy and cover-up' that let abuse stay hidden.
fixes.d: At the invitation of the Bishops' Conference of Scotland, former Church of Scotland Moderator Andrew McLellan chaired a commission reviewing the Catholic Church's safeguarding policy and practice; its 99-page report was published on 18 August 2015. It called abuse 'the greatest challenge facing the whole Catholic Church in Scotland', condemned a 'culture of secrecy and cover-up', said the Church had not made significant structural changes, and made eight key recommendations. Archbishop Philip Tartaglia offered a 'profound apology' to victims.

note: Replaced the Wikipedia url with The Tablet and CathNews. Neither contains 'most serious kind', 'culture of denial' or the naming remit, so d and cover were rewritten from what they do say.

The Scotsman confirms submission on 15 October, 114 missing/lost/destroyed files, no evidence of organised Home Office concealment, 'we cannot say that no file was removed or destroyed for that reason', nothing supporting PIE funding claims, and the Dickens letters. The 11 Nov 2014 publication date rests on the gov.uk PDF (not opened). No changes.

The Peace Archives report PDF (SEPAZ, Sept 2009) confirms the 333-file sample of 1977-1989 adoptions, army and National Police involvement in moving children, Decree 54-77 notarial adoptions without prior judicial approval, the SBS having no record of how many children it received, and abandonment declarations; UPI (12 Sept 2009) confirms Colom, Álvarez, destination countries and 'about 5,000' children among the war's disappeared. No changes.

TheJournal.ie (30 Nov 2011) confirms Raphoe: 52 allegations, 14 priests, since 1975, four convicted, Boyce's statements; Irish Times (11 Dec 2013) confirms Kerry 67/21 and Down and Connor 59/42; National Board press material confirms final reports in 2017. No changes.

fixes.d: Il Forteto, a cooperative and community at Vicchio in the Mugello near Florence, received children placed by juvenile courts and social services for decades. Its founder, Rodolfo Fiesoli, was definitively sentenced to 14 years and 10 months for abuse, although a conviction had already become final in 1985 and placements continued. Two Tuscan regional council inquiry commissions examined the case; a parliamentary inquiry in the previous legislature did not finish with a final report, and a new bicameral commission of inquiry was created by Law 47 of 25 March 2024 and installed on 1 August 2024. Its task is to establish institutional responsibilities and why authorities kept accrediting the community after court rulings on abuse and mistreatment.

note: Camera dei deputati page confirms Law 47/2024 and the commission's remit; La Nazione (1 Aug 2024) confirms Fiesoli's 14y10m final sentence, the 1985 final conviction, two regional commissions and the unfinished earlier parliamentary inquiry. Barberino di Mugello is not in the sources, so place now says Vicchio; the source does not say whose 1985 conviction it was in so wording kept general.

NOS (12 Dec 2017) confirms Klaas de Vries, set up in May, 12% and 4% survey results, 686 cases 2001-2017, 60% under 16, 70% perpetrators supervisors/coaches, 103 new reports and the proposed reporting duty. No changes.

cite: Philip Moss, Review into recent allegations relating to conditions and circumstances at the Regional Processing Centre in Nauru, published March 2015 (Al Jazeera, 21 March 2015); staff open letter, 7 April 2015, and Senate Select Committee report 'Taking responsibility', 31 August 2015 (as cited by Wikipedia)

fixes.cover: Staff wrote in an open letter in April 2015 that the Australian government had known of alleged abuses against women and children for more than 18 months
fixes.d: The Moss Review, commissioned by the Australian government and published in March 2015, was aware of three rape allegations at the Australian-run Regional Processing Centre on Nauru, one involving a minor, confirmed that a guard demanded to see a female detainee naked in exchange for extra shower time with her young child, and concluded that guards trading marijuana with detainees for sexual favours was possibly occurring. In April 2015 staff alleged multiple instances of sexual abuse of women and children in an open letter. A Senate select committee reported on 31 August 2015 in 'Taking responsibility: conditions and circumstances at Australia's Regional Processing Centre in Nauru'.

note: Al Jazeera now the main url. It does not say the marijuana-for-sex trading involved children (Wikipedia quotes that wording; SMH copy was blocked), so d now states only what Al Jazeera supports. Open letter and Senate report still rest on Wikipedia citations (url2); the APH copy could not be opened. Overlaps with x-aus-forgotten-children-2015 on the Moss Review but is a separate record.

cite: Special Court for Sierra Leone, Prosecutor v. Sesay, Kallon and Gbao (RUF case), Trial Judgment 25 February 2009; Appeal Judgment 26 October 2009 (Residual Special Court for Sierra Leone case page; UN News)

fixes.d: On 25 February 2009 the Special Court for Sierra Leone convicted RUF leaders Issa Sesay and Morris Kallon on 16 of 18 counts and Augustine Gbao on 14. All three were convicted of sexual slavery and of forced marriage as a crime against humanity, the first forced-marriage convictions by an international criminal tribunal; Sesay and Kallon were also convicted of using child soldiers, while Gbao was acquitted of that charge. They were sentenced to 52, 40 and 25 years, and on 26 October 2009 the Appeals Chamber upheld the convictions and sentences, overturning only Gbao's conviction for collective punishments.

note: Replaced Wikipedia with the Residual SCSL case page (counts, sexual slavery and forced marriage for all three, Gbao acquitted of child soldiers, sentences, 26 Oct 2009 appeal) and UN News (first international guilty verdicts for forced marriage). The rscsl page has an internal typo (2008/2009) for the trial date; 2009 is consistent with VOA.

VOA confirms 15 Mar 2018 release, title, 454 testimonies, March 2011-December 2017, rape of women and girls in detention, sexual torture of male detainees including boys, government forces and militias as worst offenders, IS forced marriages of girls and women, war crimes. No changes.

fixes.place: DR Congo (MONUSCO, 44 allegations) and other UN missions; report issued at UN Headquarters, New York
fixes.cover: About 750 paternity and child support claims against peacekeeping personnel since 2006, more than 500 still pending; claims are referred to troop-contributing countries, most of which have not taken meaningful action
fixes.d: The Secretary-General reports each year to the General Assembly on special measures for protection from sexual exploitation and abuse. The report released in March 2025 recorded 102 allegations in peacekeeping and political missions in 2024, 44 in DR Congo and 40 in the Central African Republic, with 125 victims, 27 of them children; there were also 190 allegations against staff of UN agencies, funds and programmes and 382 against staff of implementing partners. The supplementary tables list child victims in MINUSCA (Central African Republic, 13), MONUSCO (DR Congo, 9), UNMISS (South Sudan, 2), UNMIL (Liberia, 2) and UNITAD (Iraq, 1). It noted about 750 paternity claims involving peacekeepers since 2006, more than 500 still pending.

note: AP via WHQR confirms all 2024 figures and paternity claims; the UN supplementary PDF gives child victims by mission, so 'also' now lists the countries of missions with child victims (LBN, HTI, COL, AFG had only adult victims). y0/y1 set to 2024 because the figures are for 2024 ('since 2003' was not in the sources). iso3 is COD but ll is New York; owner may want ll moved to Kinshasa [15.2663, -4.4419] so the marker sits in the country of record.

fixes.cover: FBI Indianapolis officials took months to open a formal investigation, interviewed only one of three athletes (by phone), and later gave incomplete and inaccurate information to internal FBI inquiries

note: AP via OPB (14 Jul 2021) confirms the errors finding, 2015 report by USA Gymnastics, months of delay, one of three athletes interviewed by phone, inaccurate information and at least 40 girls and women over 14 months. Cover reworded to match ('did not interview two of three' kept in substance).

EWTN/CNA confirms PAC report of 20 March 2023, 28 priests credibly accused while serving in Georgia back to the 1940s, reassignment without notice, policies that 'enabled sexual abuse of minors', Savannah late 1980s and Atlanta 1990s, no case prosecutable. No changes.

Portland Press Herald (25 Feb 2004, via BishopAccountability) confirms 63 men (diocesan priests, order priests/brothers, church or school employees), 75 years, secrecy, at least seven reassigned and one later accused of abusing at least 10 girls, nothing after 1996, statute of limitations. No changes.

fixes.cover: The Attorney General cited 'flagrant indifference' to the danger posed by abusive priests and found church officials made false statements while testifying in civil suits; a December 2002 agreement let the diocese avoid criminal indictment after the AG said it had evidence likely to sustain a conviction
fixes.d: On 3 March 2003 the New Hampshire Attorney General released a 154-page report, with about 9,000 pages of supporting documents, after a 10-month investigation. It found 50 priests credibly accused of abusing minors over 60 years and cited the diocese's 'flagrant indifference' to the danger to children. Under a December 2002 agreement the diocese avoided criminal indictment, after the Attorney General said it had evidence likely to sustain a conviction against the diocese, and accepted annual monitoring by the Attorney General for at least five years.

note: Boston Globe (4 Mar 2003) confirms all figures and the agreement terms. Removed 'chose to protect itself and its priests' and 'lenient treatment' (not in the article) and attributed the 'evidence likely to sustain a conviction' statement to the AG, as the article does.

JURIST confirms a 418-page report issued on a Wednesday (21 Sept 2005), at least 63 priests, hundreds of minors over several decades, the findings on Cardinals Krol and Bevilacqua, no charges because of time limits, and the archdiocese's rejection. No changes.

fixes.cover: The report found the USOC, USA Gymnastics and other governing bodies took actions to conceal their negligence, and that the USOC and the FBI 'fundamentally failed' to protect gymnasts
fixes.d: An 18-month investigation by the Senate Commerce subcommittee led by Senators Jerry Moran and Richard Blumenthal reported on 30 July 2019. It found that the US Olympic Committee and the FBI 'fundamentally failed' to protect gymnasts from Larry Nassar, and that the USOC, USA Gymnastics and other governing bodies took actions to conceal their negligence. It found institutions repeatedly failed to report wrongdoing to law enforcement. The senators proposed the Empowering Olympic and Amateur Athletes Act to reform oversight of Olympic sport.

note: UPI confirms 18 months, Moran and Blumenthal, 260 women, concealment and failure to report. The 'fundamentally failed' finding names the USOC and FBI, not USA Gymnastics, so d and cover were corrected; added the bill's name.

CNN via WTVR confirms 233 pages, 10 Dec 2018, 100+ interviews over 10 months, Steve Penny telling Scott Blackmun and Alan Ashley in 2015, no USOC action July 2015 to Sept 2016, and Ashley fired that day. No changes.

fixes.cover: Professional deregistration of educators does not automatically lead to listing on the safeguarding register; a documented shortfall of 10,748 convicted offenders not yet entered on the National Register for Sex Offenders
fixes.d: After a complaint about alleged sexual violence by an educator at St John's College in Mthatha, Eastern Cape, the South African Human Rights Commission convened a stakeholder roundtable and on 29 June 2026 released a report describing sexual violence in schools as systemic and entrenched. It recorded 826 sexual misconduct complaints to the South African Council for Educators between 2021 and 2025 and found that professional deregistration does not automatically lead to inclusion on the safeguarding register, and that 10,748 convicted offenders had not yet been entered on the National Register for Sex Offenders.

note: SAHRC media statement (29 June 2026) confirms all figures, including 9,857 child sexual abuse cases in 2024/25. Corrected the register finding: the source says deregistration does not automatically mean listing, not that dismissals do not lead to deregistration.
